data.title: Wangiri Callback Velocity — High Volume of Short-Duration Outbound International Calls From Single Source
data.description: Detects Wangiri ("one-ring") fraud patterns where a high volume of short-duration (< 5 seconds) outbound international calls originate from a single source, indicating subscriber callbacks to premium-rate numbers. In a Wangiri scheme, fraudsters place brief inbound calls from premium-rate numbers to trigger victim callbacks. The callbacks connect to IVR systems or premium content lines that accumulate per-minute charges. This rule detects the callback side of the attack: clusters of brief outbound international calls from individual subscribers or PBX systems to premium-rate destinations. Average victim loss is $15-$50 per callback; aggregate campaign revenues reach $100K-$1M (Subex/Akamai).

detection.condition: selection AND filter_short_duration AND filter_volume AND filter_destination_diversity

enrichment_required.source: Premium-rate number range lookup table (CFCA/i3 Forum intelligence)
CDR correlation identifying prior inbound one-ring calls from the same international prefix
Country risk classification for Wangiri-target destinations

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Wangiri Callback Velocity — DL-0183")`
`comment("Detects high volume of short-duration outbound international calls")`
index=flame_telecom sourcetype=flame:cdr
  call_direction="outbound"
  call_type="international"
  call_duration_seconds < 5
| lookup premium_rate_ranges number_prefix OUTPUTNEW is_premium_rate, risk_country
| where is_premium_rate="true"
| bin _time span=24h
| stats count as short_call_count,
        dc(called_number) as unique_destinations,
        dc(destination_country) as unique_countries,
        values(called_number) as called_numbers,
        values(destination_country) as countries,
        avg(call_duration_seconds) as avg_duration,
        earliest(_time) as first_call,
        latest(_time) as last_call
  by calling_number, source_system, _time
| where short_call_count >= 10 AND unique_destinations >= 3
| eval risk_score = case(
    short_call_count >= 50 AND unique_destinations >= 10, "critical",
    short_call_count >= 25 AND unique_destinations >= 5, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table calling_number, source_system, short_call_count, unique_destinations,
        unique_countries, called_numbers, countries, avg_duration,
        first_call, last_call, risk_score
| sort - short_call_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Wangiri Callback Velocity Detection
-- Detects high volume of short-duration outbound international calls from single source
SELECT
  c.calling_number,
  c.source_system,
  COUNT(*) AS short_call_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.called_number) AS unique_destinations,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.destination_country) AS unique_countries,
  AVG(c.call_duration_seconds) AS avg_duration_seconds,
  MIN(c.call_start_time) AS first_call,
  MAX(c.call_start_time) AS last_call,
  DATEDIFF(MINUTE, MIN(c.call_start_time), MAX(c.call_start_time)) AS window_minutes,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 50 AND COUNT(DISTINCT c.called_number) >= 10 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 25 AND COUNT(DISTINCT c.called_number) >= 5 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_score
FROM call_detail_records c
JOIN premium_rate_numbers p ON c.called_number LIKE p.number_prefix || '%'
WHERE c.call_direction = 'outbound'
  AND c.call_type = 'international'
  AND c.call_duration_seconds < 5
  AND c.call_start_time >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
GROUP BY c.calling_number, c.source_system
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT c.called_number) >= 3
ORDER BY short_call_count DESC
queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Wangiri Callback Velocity
call_direction="outbound" call_type="international" call_duration_seconds < 5
| join premium_rate_numbers on called_number
| groupBy(calling_number, source_system, function=[
    count(as=short_call_count),
    countDistinct(called_number, as=unique_destinations),
    countDistinct(destination_country, as=unique_countries),
    avg(call_duration_seconds, as=avg_duration),
    min(call_start_time, as=first_call),
    max(call_start_time, as=last_call),
    collect([called_number, destination_country])
  ], span=24h)
| short_call_count >= 10
| unique_destinations >= 3
| sort(short_call_count, order=desc)

references: Subex, Global Telecom Fraud Intelligence Report (2025)
falsepositives: International business call attempts with connection failures (busy/no answer)
Automated system health checks or monitoring calls to international endpoints
Call center operations with short-duration international callback attempts
Network testing or carrier quality assurance calls
